name: Data Analysis
blurb: Profile, query, test and chart data honestly: SQL, statistics, A/B tests, pandas/Polars, sklearn, dashboards, notebooks, dbt.
searches: agent skill data analysis SQL statistics Claude
Claude skill A/B test experiment analysis
pandas Polars DuckDB new release features
data visualization dashboard skill accessibility charts

tests.prompt: Here's a CSV of our orders (order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, region, status). Give me a quick overview of the data and tell me how revenue has trended by region over the last 12 months.
tests.good: Profiles first: states grain and checks order_id uniqueness, null/placeholder values, date range and partial current month; defines revenue (e.g. completed orders only, refunds handled); excludes or labels the partial month; sums from rows not averages of averages; line chart or small multiples with an insight title, colourblind-safe palette, labelled units; notes caveats and keeps the code reproducible.

tests.prompt: We ran an A/B test on the checkout page for 9 days. Control: 10,212 users, 412 purchases. Variant: 9,604 users, 455 purchases. Did the variant win? We planned a 50/50 split.
tests.good: Runs a sample ratio mismatch check first (chi-square on 10,212 vs 9,604; p < 0.001 means the split is broken) and refuses to call a winner until it's explained; also computes conversion rates, absolute and relative difference with 95% CI and the two-proportion z-test; notes 9 days is under two full weeks; mentions the pre-planned MDE/power and guardrails; no causal claim while SRM is unresolved.

tests.prompt: Build a model to predict which customers will churn next month from our customer_monthly table (one row per customer per month with usage features and a churned flag). Accuracy is 97%, is that good?
tests.good: Points out class imbalance makes 97% accuracy meaningless; compares to a DummyClassifier baseline; uses PR AUC / recall at precision and calibration; splits by time (train on earlier months, test on later) and groups by customer so no customer leaks across; checks features are known before the prediction month; all preprocessing inside a Pipeline; picks a threshold from costs; reports importance as non-causal.

tests.prompt: Here's 18 months of our subscription data (customer_id, plan, start_date, cancel_date, mrr). Work out monthly logo and revenue churn by signup cohort, show what current churn means for our 14-month runway, and put it in a six-slide PowerPoint for Thursday's board meeting.
tests.good: States a short plan first: the analysis here (data-profiling.md, sql.md, statistics.md, visualization.md), the runway through trading-finance (startup-corporate-finance.md: burn and runway rebuilt from the churn figures, assumptions labelled), the deck through presentations (deck-story.md, data-slides.md, powerpoint-pptx.md). Defines logo and revenue churn with numerator, denominator and window; checks the customer_id grain and duplicate subscriptions; labels the partial current month; cohort chart with insight titles, colourblind-safe and not colour-only; keeps the queries reproducible; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: Our sales model is a Power BI semantic model called 'Sales' in a Fabric workspace, and I'm on a Mac. Connect Claude to it, show total sales and margin % by product category for last quarter vs the same quarter last year, and add a Margin % measure if there isn't one.
tests.good: Picks the right Power BI MCP server: the hosted Authoring endpoint (api.fabric.microsoft.com/v1/mcp/powerbi/authoring) because the local server does not run on macOS; says answers to business questions belong to Fabric IQ and the authoring server is for building the model, and Microsoft says not to register the hosted and local Authoring servers together (overlapping tools, extra tokens); it says Authoring and Fabric IQ complement each other (build the model with Authoring, then answer questions with Fabric IQ). Reword to: does not register the hosted and local Authoring servers together.; signs in through Microsoft Entra as the user with no passwords or tokens pasted into chat. Reads the model schema and lists existing tables and measures before writing DAX; checks for an existing Margin % and reuses it. Writes the ratio as DIVIDE(margin, sales) with proper time intelligence on a marked date table (DATEADD or SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR), uses the fiscal quarter, and states if the quarter is partial. Asks before changing the model: confirms the measure name, folder and format, notes it needs Write permission and that the change is hard to undo, and suggests a backup or a PBIP copy under Git. Reconciles total sales to a known report figure, mentions the 100,000-row cap on DAX results, and shows the numbers as a table with unit and period labels.

tools.name: Microsoft Excel
tools.why: Called the most-used data analysis tool in the world by 2026 tool round-ups (Futurense, Skyvia); the default hand-off format for analysts' results.

tools.name: Microsoft Power BI
tools.why: Described as the most widely deployed BI tool by user count (Domo, Futurense 2026 round-ups); Microsoft shipped hosted Authoring and Fabric IQ MCP servers and a skills repo in 2026.

tools.name: Tableau
tools.why: Named with Power BI as a leading BI tool in 2026 round-ups (Domo, Futurense); Tableau publishes an official MCP server (Apache-2.0, 348 stars) and it is listed in Claude's connector directory.

tools.name: Snowflake
tools.why: Named one of the two dominant cloud warehouses in 2026 round-ups (Domo, Skyvia); official listing in Claude's connector directory plus a Snowflake-managed MCP server.

tools.name: Google BigQuery
tools.why: Named with Snowflake as a dominant cloud warehouse (Domo, Skyvia 2026); Google ships a remote BigQuery MCP server and official skills.

tools.name: Databricks
tools.why: Lakehouse platform used with Snowflake/BigQuery at enterprise scale (Domo, Skyvia round-ups); in Claude's connector directory; official managed MCP servers for Genie, SQL and Unity Catalog.

tools.name: pandas
tools.why: Python plus pandas is named alongside SQL and Excel as the core analysis stack in 2026 round-ups (Futurense, Skyvia); pandas 3.0.6 is current.

tools.name: R and tidyverse
tools.why: R is one of the six tools named across 2026 round-ups (Futurense) and the usual choice for statisticians; Posit publishes official Claude skills (MIT, 528 stars).

tools.name: Jupyter
tools.why: The standard notebook format for Python analysis; Hex, Databricks and VS Code all open .ipynb; ranked in every analyst-tool round-up for Python work.

tools.name: dbt
tools.why: Industry-standard SQL transformation layer in modern warehouses; official dbt MCP server (607 stars) and agent skills (728 stars).

tools.name: DuckDB
tools.why: Fast-growing in-process analytics engine for local CSV/Parquet; official duckdb-skills repo (MIT, 598 stars) and an RSS feed this craft already tracks.

tools.name: Looker
tools.why: Named among the five dominant self-service BI tools (Domo 2026); Google publishes official Looker skills and supports Looker in its MCP Toolbox.

tools.name: Hex
tools.why: AI-native collaborative notebook/BI platform listed in Claude's connector directory with an official MCP server (https://app.hex.tech/mcp) and official skills.

tools.name: Google Sheets
tools.why: The spreadsheet half of the Excel/Sheets pair that most analysts hand results over in (Futurense, Skyvia round-ups); Google's Workspace CLI ships Sheets skills (31k stars).

tools.name: Qlik Sense
tools.why: A Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Analytics and BI Platforms for the 16th year (with Power BI, Tableau, Looker, ThoughtSpot, QuickSight); smaller share than Power BI/Tableau (about 2% of data-viz installs per 6sense) but a long-standing enterprise BI estate. Official remote Qlik MCP server (GA Feb 2026) with a predefined Claude client ID.

tools.name: SAS
tools.why: Still the standard in pharma and regulated work (FDA clinical submissions), banking and insurance; leads R narrowly in statistician job ads (1,040 vs 1,012, r4stats). The 'no public agent tooling' reason for leaving it out is out of date: SAS ships an official Apache-2.0 Viya MCP server (92 tools) used with Claude.

tools.name: Amplitude
tools.why: Leading product-analytics platform where funnels, retention, cohorts and experiment readouts (this craft's jobs) are run at product companies; official Claude directory connector and Amplitude-hosted MCP server (mcp.amplitude.com/mcp, OAuth). No neighbouring craft lists it.

tools.name: Mixpanel
tools.why: The other big product-analytics tool beside Amplitude; listed in Claude's connector directory with a Mixpanel-hosted MCP server (70+ tools: insights, funnels, flows, retention, cohorts, experiments). No neighbouring craft lists it.
